svg.text: Modular monolith · four bounded contexts · dependency always pointing inward · boundaries checked by tooling, not by agreement
The first import is config: it validates the environment and throws. A process that starts without DATABASE_URL finds out in the middle of an enrollment.
Bun.serve({ fetch: app.fetch }) · startScheduler([sessionPurge]) — the only point outside web that calls a module directly
SIGTERM/SIGINT: stop accepting → drain what is in flight → close the pool. In that order, so the queue does not grow while draining.
Interface (delivery) — src/web/ : HTTP in, HTML out. No business rule lives here.
Hono. The chain order is the semantics:
onError repeats the error middleware because
Hono will not let the exception reach next().
7 routers mounted by prefix: login, account,
the compiler enforces :params, the .eta does not.
Idempotency only on the groups that write.
Eta with autoEscape: interpolating user data is
safe by default, and "~" becomes a visible decision.
45 .eta files. One function builds every page and
injects session, idempotency key, ROUTES and the
Modules — four bounded contexts in the same process. Each has its domain, its application and its infra; none sees inside another.

Shared kernel — src/shared/ : infrastructure with no business rule. The arrow never goes from here up into a module.
infrastructure — open to application/ and infra/, closed to the domain
application/ and infra/ use everything here
PostgreSQL — 18 tables, 16 of them scoped by network_id
identity: network, school, app_user, user_role, session · academics: academic_year, subject, class_group,
class_group_subject, student, student_guardian, enrollment · assessment: grade, attendance,
term_closing · communication: announcement, announcement_recipient · platform: idempotent_request (no network_id)
public/ — assets with the hash in the name
app.<hash>.css generated by bun run build:assets.
The name carries the content, so a one-year
Bun.sql · transaction opened in one place only
identity is the leaf: it knows nobody — and that is why
the other three are allowed to point at it.
Every arrow crosses through index.ts. domain/, application/ and infra/ are private.
Three rules that `bun run check` rejects — config/.dependency-cruiser.js
A module only sees another through index.ts. An internal path
is private. It is what gives "what else touches this?" an
answer: when billing/ is extracted at S14, the list of
dependents is exactly whoever imports the index — without it,
the extraction turns into a rewrite.
The domain does not know a database, HTTP, log, scheduler or
third-party library exists. It only reaches ports/, result.ts
and document/. That is what makes a rule test a pure test.
Dependency always points inward: shared/ imports no context at
all. That is why shared/http/session.ts declares the shape of
the user instead of importing it from identity.
Decisions the blueprint does not show on its own
unitOfWork() is the application's only commit point. The outbox INSERT,
when it exists, goes in there and nowhere else.
reader() and writer() are already distinct functions over a single pool.
Switching to the replica at S08 touches no repository.
The key comes from the application
uuidIdGenerator produces the UUID: parent and child in the same transaction,
with no round trip to learn the parent's id.
bun run verify = typecheck → check (depcruise) → magic (literals with no
owner) → test. None of the four is optional.
solid arrow — a real import, checked at compile time
dashed arrow — application/ calls the repositories in infra/
arrow rejected by depcruise: the build breaks if anyone tries
The colours say the layer, not the module:
facade — the bounded context's only door
application — orchestrates, validates, opens the transaction
domain — thick border: the core, framework-free
ports — what the domain is allowed to know
The blueprint is Stage 01's. It was already drawn with S14 in mind.
